audit_findings.title: The post-year-end MLTP joint venture may invalidate the perimeter and introduce an unallocated NCI claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.151 million NCI, equal to $0.23 per share and 0.4% of base equity value; $157.839 million purchase consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: The missing NCI deduction overstates the equity bridge, while anchoring OE to pre-acquisition 2025 results excludes MLTP earnings and may understate operating value. The post-closing cash balance already reflects acquisition funding.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the agreement, MultiLane will contribute all the assets related to its test and measurement business to the joint venture and we will invest approximately $157 million in exchange for 75% ownership of MLTP.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that MLTP closed on April 8, 2026, is consolidated, and is only 75% owned, so the null perimeter is an error. The recorded NCI claim is only $36.151 million versus $8.980 billion of base equity value. Teradyne also states that MLTP's standalone financial-statement contribution was not material. Correcting the known bridge defect would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $355.77 market price.
audit_findings.action: Define MLTP in the perimeter, confirm that the June 2026 cash balance includes the acquisition payment, deduct the $36.151 million NCI from the bridge, and allocate 25% of MLTP earnings to NCI whenever post-closing OE is introduced.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement and deferred-compensation claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $139.296 million net recorded position, equal to $0.88 per share and 1.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retirement deficit not already discharged through projected OE is a claim ahead of common equity and should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The liability for the U.S. Supplemental Savings Plan at December 31, 2025, and 2024 , was $ 71.7 million and $ 63.4 million, respectively, and is included in retirement plan liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: At June 28, 2026, filed retirement-plan liabilities were $151.436 million and retirement-plan assets were $12.140 million, producing a maximum recorded net position of $139.296 million. Deducting that entire amount would reduce base value from $56.53 to about $55.65 per share, still far below the $355.77 market price. The full deduction may overstate the correction if projected OE already includes future contributions.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $151.436 million liability by plan against the $12.140 million asset and forecast contributions, identify payments already captured in OE, and rerun the bridge deducting only the uncovered claim.

audit_findings.title: Large non-cancelable purchase commitments could create an unrecorded onerous operating claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (gross commitments are $1,781.4 million, including $1,558.8 million within one year, but the loss-bearing portion is not filed)
audit_findings.mechanism: Cancellation penalties, purchases exceeding usable demand, or unusable components would reduce future OE through inventory provisions, lower margins, or a direct bridge liability.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase commitments covered by the agreements aggregate to approximately $ 1,473.0 million, of which $ 1,415.1 million is for less than one year.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are contractual and equal to more than three times 2025 OE, but their gross amount is not an economic loss because components used in saleable products flow through ordinary working capital and cost of revenue. The record does not disclose backlog coverage, cancellation economics, or unavoidable excess, so it cannot establish whether the onerous portion is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain commitment-level cancellation rights, penalties, component usability, current backlog coverage, and demand forecasts; quantify unavoidable excess cost and rerun OE or the bridge for that amount.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value may perpetuate a tax benefit that expires when the terminal period begins
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.6 million annual 2025 benefit; conservative full-horizon removal would reduce base value by about $303.5 million or $1.91 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized tax benefit raises OE and, if carried beyond 2035, is capitalized in the terminal value beginning in 2036.
audit_findings.evidence: The new tax holiday is scheduled to expire on December 31, 2035.
audit_findings.explanation: The forecast timing places year 10 in 2035 and the terminal period in 2036, when the holiday has expired. The valuation does not state that terminal taxes were normalized, so the issue is unresolved. As a conservative scale test, removing the entire $21.6 million benefit from the anchor and every forecast year would lower base value from $56.53 to about $54.62 per share; an expiry-only correction would be smaller and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Explicitly retain the holiday only through 2035, apply the normalized post-holiday tax rate and applicable QDMTT from 2036, and rerun year 11 and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Technoprobe may be represented both in owner earnings and as a separately added stake
audit_findings.magnitude: If retained, the filed 2025 loss of $19.914 million implies about $279.8 million or $1.76 per share of base operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income or loss and basis-difference amortization must be removed from OE when the Technoprobe stake is separately added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Teradyne records its share of Technoprobe's net income or loss and the amortization of equity method basis difference, as 'Equity in net earnings of affiliate' in the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that GAAP net income contains Technoprobe results, including losses of $19.914 million in 2025 and $7.211 million in 2024, but the record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation purged them. If the 2025 loss remains in the $571.8 million anchor, removing it would increase base value from $56.53 to about $58.29 per share. That does not change the valuation conclusion, although the direction could reverse in future profitable affiliate periods if the structural mismatch persists.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE year to the equity-in-net-earnings line, remove all Technoprobe income or loss and basis-difference amortization, retain only the separately valued $591 million stake in the bridge, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.
